newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures slash losses late, end weaker.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures slash losses late, end weaker.

text.p: A late bout of loss-cutting hoisted U.S. debt futures back up toward unchanged, although most units still ended on the minus side.
June U.S. Treasury bond futures set the pit-session peak at 108-24/32 late as shorts covered and dealers bought size.

Brokers characterized the comeback largely as a reaction to the contract's ability to test and hold the 108-06/32 - 07/32 area, roughly seven percent cash yield. The latter price also matched the six-month low hit in late September.
"It was a technical bounce. You had the street buying it," one floor broker said of the late comeback in nearby T-bonds.

Futures had eroded most of the morning, hitting price troughs after midday when comments by San Francisco Federal Reserve president Robert Parry gave sellers the excuse they had sought to test the seven percent yield level.
"I think Parry was part of the reason we came off a bit," said a Eurodollar broker. "We hit our lows when he spoke."
Parry spooked traders by saying it is "absolutely essential" the Fed be forward looking in its fight against inflation.
"I don't see the inflation signs, but I see the factors that precede an increase in inflation," Parry said.
But futures began working back up after respecting support as traders turned attention to fundamentals facing the market.

Tuesday's February U.S. housing starts are forecast rising to a 1.45 million unit rate from 1.35 million units. Wednesday's February consumer price index is expected to gain 0.2 percent overall and in the core rate.

Fed chairman Alan Greenspan also will speak on two separate occasions this week. On Wednesday, he discusses financial services modernization before a House committee. On Thursday he testifies to the Joint Economic Committee about monetary policy and interest rates.

The technical outlook for the next few weeks still remained biased to the downside, with chartists calling Monday's partial recovery insufficient to erase the bearish undertones. But they did not rule out slightly more upside left from Monday's bounce.
"It depends on two things: the numbers tomorrow and what Greenspan says," said the T-bond futures floor broker.

June T-bonds ended down 3/32 at 108-24/32, T-notes lost 4/32 to 106-22/32, muni bonds added 3/32 to 112-27/32, September T-bills lost 0.025 bps to 94.470, and Eurodollars lost 0.025 bps to 93.910. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
